claim: Bulk whole genome sequencing (WGS) can only identify old mutational events due to depth limitations.
source: Bulk whole genome sequencing (WGS) enables the analysis of tumor evolution but, because of depth limitations, can only identify old mutational events.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a limitation of bulk WGS.

claim: Discovery of current mutational processes requires dense sequencing of individual clones or single cells.
source: The discovery of current mutational processes for predicting the tumor's evolutionary trajectory requires dense sequencing of individual clones or single cells.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement in the abstract.

claim: Single cell and small clone sequencing studies are problematic due to excessive false positive mutations when sequencing picogram quantities of DNA.
source: Such studies, however, are inherently problematic because of the discovery of excessive false positive (FP) mutations when sequencing picogram quantities of DNA.
evidence: This is stated as a known problem in the abstract.

claim: DigiPico/MutLX virtually eliminates all false positive results while retaining an excellent proportion of true positives.
source: Here we report a robust WGS and analysis pipeline (DigiPico/MutLX) that virtually eliminates all F results while retaining an excellent proportion of true positives.
evidence: This is the main claim of the paper stated in the abstract.

claim: A hyper-mutation (kataegis) event was identified for the first time in a group of ~30 cancer cells from a recurrent ovarian carcinoma using DigiPico/MutLX.
source: Using our method, we identified, for the first time, a hyper-mutation (kataegis) event in a group of ∼30 cancer cells from a recurrent ovarian carcinoma.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the abstract.

claim: The kataegis event identified was unidentifiable from bulk WGS data.
source: This was unidentifiable from the bulk WGS data.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a comparison to bulk sequencing.

claim: Standard bulk WGS approaches can only detect highly prevalent mutations that occurred early in tumorigenesis.
source: However, the limitation of the depth of sequencing means that only highly prevalent mutations that occurred early in tumorigenesis can be detected using standard bulk whole genome sequencing (WGS) approaches (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by figures.

claim: The ability to model evolutionary events from bulk WGS is limited to early events that have been fixed during tumor evolution and not recent or current processes.
source: Consequently, the ability to model evolutionary events is limited to early events that have been fixed during the tumor evolution and not recent or current processes (Turajlic et al., 2019; Barber et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation with supporting citations.

claim: Studying current or recent evolutionary events requires confident identification of mutations with very low prevalence.
source: Studying current or recent evolutionary events requires the confident identification of mutations with very low prevalence (Turajlic et al., 2019; Barber et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a requirement with supporting citations.

claim: Unavoidable DNA damage through oxidation or spontaneous deamination is particularly troublesome when dealing with small quantities of DNA.
source: Unavoidable DNA damage through oxidation or spontaneous deamination is particularly troublesome when dealing with small quantities of DNA (Bohrson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a known problem with citation support.

claim: DNA damage results in disproportionate numbers of artefactual C > A and C > T mutations.
source: These sources of damage result in disproportionate numbers of artefactual C > A and C > T mutations, respectively (Bohrson et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2017a; Costello et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citation support.

claim: It is not currently possible to differentiate between biologically-driven C > A and C > T mutations and artefactual ones when working with picogram quantities of DNA.
source: It is not currently possible to differentiate between biologically-driven C > A and C > T mutations and the artefactual ones that have arisen during library preparation when working with picogram quantities of DNA.
evidence: This is stated as a current limitation in the field.

claim: Whole genome amplification (WGA) inflates the number of artefactual mutations and propagates errors caused by DNA damage.
source: In addition, the usual step of whole genome amplification (WGA) prior to sequencing inflates the number of artefactual mutations and propagates the errors caused by DNA damage (Bohrson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a known problem with citation support.

claim: Amplification errors occur at random during the amplification process.
source: A key feature of amplification errors with or without prior DNA damage is that they are introduced at random during the amplification process (Chen et al., 2017a; Costello et al., 2013; Arbeithuber et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a key feature with citation support.

claim: When amplifying and sequencing a single DNA molecule, an artefactual mutation would be present in only a fraction of the reads.
source: We, therefore, hypothesized that when amplifying and sequencing a single DNA molecule an artefactual mutation would be present in only a fraction of the reads that have resulted from sequencing the original single DNA molecule.
evidence: This is stated as the authors' hypothesis.

claim: Genuine variants would be expected to be present in all reads from a single DNA molecule.
source: In contrast, genuine variants would be expected to be present in all such reads.
evidence: This is stated as a contrasting expectation to artefactual mutations.

claim: Partitioning template DNA into individual compartments prior to WGA enables identification of artefactual mutations.
source: Partitioning of the template DNA into individual compartments prior to WGA, such that each compartment receives no more than one DNA molecule from every locus would result in such single DNA molecule sequencing data (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as the method's approach with figure support.

claim: DigiPico library preparation distributes nearly 200 pg of DNA into individual wells of a 384-well plate.
source: To perform DigiPico sequencing, first, we uniformly distribute nearly 200 pg of DNA (obtained from 20 to 30 human cells) into individual wells of a 384-well plate.
evidence: This is stated as part of the DigiPico method description.

claim: The likelihood for co-presence of two different DNA molecules from the same locus in the same well is less than 10% in DigiPico.
source: This ensures that the likelihood for the co-presence of two different DNA molecules from the same locus in the same well is less than 10% (Peters et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the partitioning strategy with citation.

claim: REPLI-g Single Cell amplification was the only MDA method that met the required sensitivity and selectivity for DigiPico.
source: Comparing six different MDA strategies, REPLI-g Single Cell amplification was the only method that met the required sensitivity and selectivity for our purpose (Figure 1F; Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result of comparing different methods with figure support.

claim: DigiPico library D1110 had an overall mapping rate of 91.35% on human hg19 genome.
source: The initial assessment of the obtained sequencing data revealed that both the D1110 and D1111 libraries have resulted in high quality sequencing data with an overall mapping rate of 91.35% and 94.27% on human hg19 genome, respectively (Figure 1G;; Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: DigiPico library D1111 had an overall mapping rate of 94.27% on human hg19 genome.
source: The initial assessment of the obtained sequencing data revealed that both the D1110 and D1111 libraries have resulted in high quality sequencing data with an overall mapping rate of 91.35% and 94.27% on human hg19 genome, respectively (Figure 1G;; Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: Run D1110 achieved a breadth of coverage of 92.1% with a depth of 30x.
source: This cumulatively resulted in a breadth of coverage of 92.1% and 91.1% with a depth of 30x and 43x for each run, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a result for run D1110.

claim: Run D1111 achieved a breadth of coverage of 91.1% with a depth of 43x.
source: This cumulatively resulted in a breadth of coverage of 92.1% and 91.1% with a depth of 30x and 43x for each run, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a result for run D1111.

claim: UTD variants in run D1110 had significantly higher proportion of dual-allelic compartments compared to other mutation categories.
source: Comparing the frequency of wells with co-presence of two allele for the same locus (Figure 2A) as well as the number of wells supporting each variant (Figure 2B) in run D1110 showed that UTDs had significantly higher proportion of the former and lower number of the latter compared to any other category of mutations (p<2e-16 for both analyses, One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD testing).
evidence: This is stated as a statistical result with figure support.

claim: UTD variants in run D1110 were present in significantly fewer wells compared to other mutation categories.
source: Comparing the frequency of wells with co-presence of two allele for the same locus (Figure 2A) as well as the number of wells supporting each variant (Figure 2B) in run D1110 showed that UTDs had significantly higher proportion of the former and lower number of the latter compared to any other category of mutations (p<2e-16 for both analyses, One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD testing).
evidence: This is stated as a statistical result with figure support.

claim: MutLX eliminated over 99% of false positive variant calls in runs D1110, DE011, and GM12885.
source: However, the application of MutLX algorithm on the UTD variants of runs D1110, DE011, and GM12885 resulted in the effective elimination of over 99% of the FP variant calls in these runs to only 4, 7, and three genome-wide FP mutations, respectively, while maintaining a sensitivity of ∼85% for detecting true mutations (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: MutLX maintained a sensitivity of approximately 85% for detecting true mutations.
source: However, the application of MutLX algorithm on the UTD variants of runs D1110, DE011, and GM12885 resulted in the effective elimination of over 99% of the FP variant calls in these runs to only 4, 7, and three genome-wide FP mutations, respectively, while maintaining a sensitivity of ∼85% for detecting true mutations (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: SCcaller analysis resulted in 713, 712, and 13,280 false positive variant calls for runs D1110, DE011, and GM12885 respectively.
source: In comparison, SCcaller (Dong et al., 2017) analysis of the same data resulted in 713, 712, and 13,280 FP variant calls, respectively (Figure 2G; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison result with figure support.

claim: MutLX identified 266 putative clone-specific variants in run D1111, of which 240 (90%) were validated.
source: On the other hand, MutLX identified 266 putative clone-specific variants in run D1111, 240 of which (90%) were validated through comparison with independent high-depth datasets of this tumor sample (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: Out of 11 analyzed amplicons harboring clone-specific variants from run D1111, 10 were found to be present at low frequencies in the bulk DNA of the PT2R sample.
source: Moreover, these observations were further validated by performing targeted sequencing on the bulk DNA of the tumor. Whereby, out of the 11 analyzed amplicons harboring clone-specific variants from run D1111, 10 were found to conclusively be present at low frequencies in the bulk DNA of the PT2R sample (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result.

claim: Amplicon sequencing of 37 UTD variants from run DE111 labeled as artefactual by MutLX showed no evidence for their presence in the bulk DNA sample.
source: Furthermore, amplicon sequencing of 37 seemingly high-quality UTD variants from run DE111 that were labelled as artefactual by MutLX algorithm indicated no evidence for their presence in the bulk DNA sample (Figure 2—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result.

claim: A UTD*/UTD ratio as high as 10% does not significantly affect the recovery rate of UTD* variants in MutLX.
source: The results showed that a UTD*/UTD ratio as high as 10% does not significantly affect the recovery rate of UTD* variants, indicating that overfitting does not occur in MutLX (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from simulated data with figure support.

claim: There is a higher level of C > A mutations among identified artefactual mutations, consistent with oxidative damage to template DNA.
source: Importantly, analyzing the frequency of different mutation types in these data indicated the presence of a higher level of C > A mutations among the identified artefactual mutations, consistent with the notion that such FP calls are a result of oxidative damage to the template DNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Figure 2—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support and interpretation.

claim: 84.6% of somatic mutations identified in bulk pre-chemotherapy sequencing data were present in at least three tumor islets from DigiPico data.
source: The analysis of the bulk pre-chemotherapy sequencing data identified 13,721 somatic mutations. 84.6% of these mutations were present in at least three tumor islets from DigiPico data, 91.4% of which were also present in at least three additional islets from previously published LFR data (Hellner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a result from patient #11152 analysis.

claim: The five pre-chemotherapy islets harbored 2, 6, 8, 8, and 36 truly unique mutations respectively.
source: Each of the five pre-chemotherapy islets harbored a number of truly unique mutations (2, 6, 8, 8, and 36), compared to other islets, indicating that they were recent occurrences (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: The bulk WGS data of the PT2R recurrence indicated the emergence of 3009 new somatic mutations absent in pre-chemotherapy data.
source: The bulk WGS data of the PT2R recurrence indicated the emergence of 3009 new somatic mutations that were absent in the pre-chemotherapy bulk sequencing data, DigiPico data or LFR data.
evidence: This is stated as a result from patient #11152 analysis.

claim: The pelvic recurrent tumor (PT2R) has a high load of clone-specific mutations compared to the para-aortic lymph node recurrence (PALNR) or the pre-chemotherapy tumor.
source: The analysis of tumor islets in the recurrence samples from patient #11152 showed that the pelvic recurrent tumor (PT2R) has a high load of clone-specific mutations compared to the para-aortic lymph node recurrence (PALNR) or the pre-chemotherapy tumor.
evidence: This is stated as a result from patient #11152 analysis.

claim: A strong sub-clonal local hyper-mutagenesis (kataegis) event was identified on chromosome 17 in the PT2R sample.
source: Moreover, analyzing the clone-specific mutations of the PT2R sample with a rainfall plot revealed the presence of a strong sub-clonal local hyper-mutagenesis (kataegis) event (Nik-Zainal et al., 2012) on chromosome 17 (Figure 3B,C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result with figure support.

claim: The mutations making up the kataegis event were only found in the DigiPico PT2R data, indicating they were genuine clone-specific mutations.
source: Comparing the mutations that made up this kataegis events to bulk sequencing data, DigiPico data and LFR data of the pre-chemotherapy omental mass revealed that they were only found in the DigiPico PT2R data indicating that they were genuine clone-specific mutations.
evidence: This is stated as a validation result.

claim: DigiPico/MutLX is compatible with genomes that suffer from extensive copy number alterations, such as in HGSOC.
source: Moreover, unlike other computational methods that rely on diploid regions of the genome to calculate amplification biases, our method is also compatible with genomes that suffer from extensive copy number alterations, such as in HGSOC.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method in the discussion.

claim: The additional processing steps required for DigiPico library preparation add nearly £250 to the total reagent costs.
source: The additional processing steps required for the DigiPico library preparation, at present, adds nearly £250 to the total reagent costs.
evidence: This is stated as a cost consideration in the methods.

claim: Artificial neural networks have shown to be capable of extracting complex patterns from high-dimensional inputs.
source: Since ANNs have shown to be capable of extracting complex patterns from high-dimensional inputs, they make a good candidate for identifying and eliminating FP mutations from this type of data.
evidence: This is stated as justification for using ANNs.

claim: Artefactual mutations result in compartments with reads supporting multiple alleles.
source: Since the artefactual mutations would result in compartments with reads supporting multiple alleles this approach enables the identification of these artefacts and allows for the elimination of FP variant calls.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the partitioning approach.

claim: Genuine variants are expected to be regularly present across replicates while artefactual mutations will have limited presence in a small number of compartments.
source: While genuine variants are expected to be regularly present across replicates, the artefactual mutations, because of their stochastic nature, will likely have a limited presence in a small number of compartments.
evidence: This is stated as an expected pattern difference.

claim: EvaGreen is an intercalating dye that binds to the minor groove of DNA and does not interfere with isothermal WGA reactions.
source: EvaGreen is an intercalating dye that binds to the minor groove of the DNA and therefore, does not interfere with the isothermal WGA reactions (Hosokawa et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a property of EvaGreen with citation.

claim: The tumor sample from patient #11152 was the most extensively whole genome sequenced tumor to date with approximately 4200x total depth from 48 independent WGS datasets.
source: This is because these DigiPico runs had been obtained from a HGSOC (High-grade Serous Ovarian Cancer) that was previously extensively sequenced with data available from 48 independent WGS data sets across three different time points (patient #11152) at a total depth of approximately 4200x from two independent sequencing platforms (Hellner et al., 2016). To our knowledge, this comprises the most extensively whole genome sequenced tumor to date.
evidence: This is stated as a claim about the dataset used for validation.

claim: MutLX employs a two-step training process to accommodate for noise in the training dataset.
source: To accommodate for this type of noise in the training dataset we employed a two-step training process (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated as part of the MutLX method description.

claim: In the first training step, mutations that appear to have been mislabeled are temporarily eliminated from the dataset.
source: In the first step, a model is trained given all labelled example data. This initial model is then used to compute the probability of each mutation belonging to its label's category. Any mutation that appears to have been mislabeled based on these model predictions, is temporarily eliminated (pruned) from the dataset.
evidence: This is stated as part of the MutLX training process.

claim: A robust prediction is supported by most of the activated neurons in the hidden layers of the ANN.
source: This uncertainty estimation is based on the assumption that a robust prediction is supported by most of the activated neurons in the hidden layers of the ANN.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption underlying the uncertainty estimation.

claim: DigiPico sequencing can produce high-quality sequencing data with excellent coverage from limited amounts of frozen clinical samples.
source: These results confirmed that DigiPico sequencing can be used to produce high-quality sequencing data with excellent coverage from limited amount of frozen clinical samples.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the quality assessment results.

claim: Nearly all UTD variants in D1110 DigiPico run ought to be artefacts.
source: Consequently, given that the standard bulk sequencing data of the PT2R sample had been obtained from the same DNA extract that was used for D1110 library preparation, nearly all the UTD variants in D1110 DigiPico run ought to be artefacts (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated as a logical consequence of the experimental design.

claim: The UTDs in run D1111 are likely to contain some clone-specific mutations alongside artefactual mutations.
source: To the contrary, the UTDs in run D1111 are likely to contain some clone-specific mutations alongside the artefactual mutations (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated as an expectation based on the experimental design.

claim: MutLX can learn accurate classification models that distinguish artefactual mutations from real variants.
source: These results clearly confirm that MutLX can learn accurate classification models that distinguish artefactual mutations from real variants and is able to effectively identify true clone-specific variants in DigiPico data.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the validation results.

claim: MutLX can reliably identify and eliminate artefactual variant calls from a diverse set of DigiPico libraries.
source: The results clearly indicate that MutLX can reliably identify and eliminate the artefactual variant calls from a diverse set of DigiPico libraries (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from testing on multiple samples.

claim: Understanding current mutational processes is key for predicting the evolutionary trajectory of a tumor.
source: Understanding current mutational processes is key for predicting the evolutionary trajectory of a tumor and, potentially, for interfering with such trajectories therapeutically.
evidence: This is stated as a motivation in the discussion.

claim: A mutation identified in bulk sequencing must have occurred at a point during the extended history of a tumor from initiation till presentation.
source: A mutation that is identified in bulk sequencing of a tumor must have occurred at a point during the extended history of a tumor from the initiation till presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a logical consequence of bulk sequencing.

claim: A cell-specific mutation must have occurred during the limited lifetime of that cell.
source: In contrast, a cell-specific mutation must have occurred during the limited lifetime of that cell.
evidence: This is stated as a logical consequence of cell-specific mutations.

claim: Current methods for single cell WGS analysis either require extensive validation studies or rely on combining data from multiple cells.
source: To overcome significant technical pitfalls predominantly related to the discovery of FP mutations, current methods for single cell WGS analysis either require extensive validation studies (Dong et al., 2017) or rely on combining data from multiple cells to obtain reliable mutations that are shared between cells (Zafar et al., 2016; Laks et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current methods with citations.

claim: Reducing the depth of sequencing per cell to enable sequencing large numbers of cells reduces the breadth of coverage.
source: Furthermore, reducing the depth of sequencing per cell to enable sequencing large numbers of cells, reduces the breadth of coverage, which is already compromised by loss of genetic materials during preparation steps.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of current approaches.

claim: DigiPico/MutLX has the distinct advantage of enabling the preservation of spatial information.
source: DigiPico/MutLX has the distinct advantage of enabling the preservation of spatial information.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method.

claim: Analyzing spatially-related cells enables the assumption that physically related cells belong to an individual clone.
source: Analyzing spatially-related cells, preserves physical relatedness and enables the assumption that physically related cells belong to an individual clone (Martincorena et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a benefit of preserving spatial information with citation.
